periods.analysis: Naloxone distribution began with 210 kits, and prevention and treatment information is stocked at nine locations. Employer outreach is off to a slow start, with few seaport businesses answering in the winter.
periods.recommendations: Use the Seaport Workers Clinic to set up employer meetings and add racks at urgent care clinics.

periods.analysis: Kits distributed rose to 395 and stocked locations to 15. Listening sessions in East Flats and Riverside surfaced cost and work schedules as the main barriers to treatment. Employer briefings picked up, though seaport businesses remain hard to schedule.
periods.recommendations: Run the recovery month series and overdose awareness events, and ask clinics to respond to the schedule barrier.

periods.analysis: Public education sessions, materials placement and naloxone training all moved forward in Q3, helped by the late-summer overdose awareness campaign. Employer and faith partner outreach is progressing more slowly than the rest. Resident feedback on barriers to treatment is now shaping where we place materials and which hours clinics offer walk-in access.
periods.recommendations: Recruit employers with shift-friendly formats and place public naloxone cabinets.
